text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Vienna bourse announced plans to form a shareholder company to manage all trading operations, so raising efficiency and cutting costs, and also introduce a market segment for smaller firms.

- German car maker Audi may give Steyr-Daimler-Puch Fahrzeugtechnik an order to produce its first three-litre-car in Graz, southern Austria. Audi chief Herbert Demel sees Austria as an important production location.
- Grocery chain Spar has taken over all of Swiss Migros' Austrian familia shops.
- Prices for diesel and heating oil have been lowered by up to 0.25 schillings.
- Consultants Frost & Sullivan expect Austrian ecologically friendly sales to triple by 2002.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima said it would be a catastrophe for Austria's economy should the country not make it into the European Monetary Union in the first round.
- Klima and Social Affairs Minister Franz Hums want higher taxes for high income earners. Up to 15 billion schillings from tax income could be allocated for welfare.
- Austria's unemployment rate at 4.1 percent is third only to Japan and Luxembourg among all OECD countries
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank (RZB) is interested in participating in soon-to-be-privatised savings bank PSK. RZB expects its own operating profits up 15 percent in 1996.
- Fireproof maker Veitsch-Radex is expanding its capacities in Turkey after only recently opening a factory in China. Investments will total some 600 million schillings this year.

- Market speculation has RZB taking over Die Erste savings bank's stake in GiroCredit, while the latter will receive control of PSK. Die Erste could then invest five to six billion schillings in Creditanstalt, making it the strongest player in the consortium around EA-Generali.

- Some 69 percent of Austrians are against an expansion of the European Union eastwards, a study by the European Commission says. A common security policy is approved of by the majority of the population.
- Finance ministry says four or five parties are interested in taking over the government's stake in Creditanstalt.
